question: In a pedigree of an autosomal dominant trait it is observed that:

options.opa: The trait appears more frequently in males.
options.opb: The unaffected people do not transmit the trait.
options.opc: The trait tends to skip generations.
options.opd: The affected people have both affected parents.
options.ope: The trait tends to appear in the progeny of related parents.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait typically appears in every generation" -> "unaffected individuals do not transmit the trait" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait can be passed from affected parent to child" -> "trait does not skip generations" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait can be expressed in both sexes" -> "no significant male predominance" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "affected individuals can have unaffected parents" -> "trait can appear due to new mutations" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "increased risk of trait in progeny of related parents" -> "inbreeding increases likelihood of expression" -> 75%
analysis: In a pedigree of an autosomal dominant trait, it is typically observed that unaffected individuals do not transmit the trait, as the trait requires only one copy of the dominant allele to be expressed. Therefore, option 'opb' is correct. The other options do not accurately describe the inheritance pattern of autosomal dominant traits.
